description: Original introductory single-item conceptual checks for selected concepts. They sample understanding but do not establish mastery. No check exists for every concept.

questions.prompt: A function assigns each allowed input…
choices: exactly one output
at least two different outputs
one output only when the input is positive
questions.feedback: A function can map different inputs to the same value, but each input in its domain has exactly one assigned output.

questions.prompt: What does lim(x→a) f(x)=L say?
choices: Values of f(x) approach L as x approaches a; f(a) need not equal L
f(a) must be defined and equal L
f(x) is constant near a
questions.feedback: A limit describes nearby behavior and does not alone establish the value at the point.

questions.prompt: On a position–time graph, instantaneous velocity at a time is…
choices: the slope of the tangent at that time
the height of the graph at that time
the average position over the full journey
questions.feedback: When the position is differentiable, velocity is its derivative, represented by the tangent slope.

questions.prompt: Two perpendicular velocity components are 3 m/s and 4 m/s. What is the resulting speed?
choices: 5 m/s
7 m/s
1 m/s
questions.feedback: Perpendicular components combine by the Pythagorean theorem: √(3²+4²)=5 m/s.

questions.prompt: If the total external force on a system is zero, its total linear momentum…
choices: remains constant
must be zero
necessarily increases
questions.feedback: With zero net external force, the time derivative of total momentum vanishes; the momentum can be nonzero.

questions.prompt: Two mutually exclusive events A and B each have probability 0.2. What is P(A or B)?
questions.feedback: For mutually exclusive events the overlap has probability zero, so their probabilities add.

questions.prompt: For a continuous random variable, the probability at one exact value is generally…
choices: zero even when its probability density there is positive
equal to its density at that point
always one
questions.feedback: A continuous variable has probability determined by area over an interval. Density is not itself point probability.

questions.prompt: What is a typical purpose of Monte Carlo simulation?
choices: Estimate quantities using random samples from a specified model
Prove that every sampled outcome must occur in nature
Replace all model assumptions with observed facts
questions.feedback: Monte Carlo draws samples from a chosen stochastic model to estimate quantities; the results depend on that model.

questions.prompt: A body with zero net force can…
choices: move at constant nonzero velocity
only remain at rest
accelerate continuously
questions.feedback: Zero net force implies zero acceleration in an inertial frame; constant nonzero velocity is possible.

questions.prompt: In the ideal isolated Newtonian two-body problem, what produces the bodies' mutual accelerations?
choices: their gravitational interaction
a third body's required gravitational pull
the orbital path itself without any force
questions.feedback: The two bodies accelerate under their mutual gravitational attraction; a third body is not required.

questions.prompt: A star's main-sequence phase is primarily associated with…
choices: hydrogen fusion in its core
all nuclear fusion stopping
the formation of a neutron star
questions.feedback: A main-sequence star is characterized by core hydrogen burning, with details depending on mass and composition.

questions.prompt: A core-collapse supernova typically involves…
choices: the gravitational collapse of a massive star's core
two ordinary stars merely passing each other
a main-sequence star having no nuclear reactions
questions.feedback: Core collapse occurs when the core of a sufficiently evolved massive star loses support; not every collapse yields an identical explosion.

questions.prompt: Why can the direction of a natal kick matter for a surviving binary?
choices: It changes the remnant's velocity vector relative to its companion
Direction cannot affect orbital energy
It changes the companion's mass by definition
questions.feedback: The kick adds a velocity vector to the remnant; its direction relative to prior orbital motion can influence binding and orbital shape.

questions.prompt: A binary population-synthesis model primarily…
choices: evolves a set of modeled binary systems under selected physical assumptions
directly observes every binary in the universe
eliminates uncertainty about binary evolution
questions.feedback: Population synthesis predicts outcomes for assumed initial populations and evolutionary prescriptions; it does not directly observe all systems.

questions.prompt: An event table shows binary identifiers 8, 8, and 15. How many distinct binaries appear?
questions.feedback: There are three event rows but only two unique identifiers: 8 and 15.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a row from a column in a typical scientific data table?
choices: A row represents one record and a column a recorded variable
A row is always one unique physical system
A column must contain only dates
questions.feedback: Rows are records and columns are variables. A single system may have many rows when events or time samples are recorded.

questions.prompt: If a detector is more sensitive to some sources than others, the detected population…
choices: may differ systematically from the underlying population
must have the same distribution as all sources
contains only systems with the smallest possible mass
questions.feedback: Detection efficiency can vary by source properties, so comparisons with model populations should account for selection.

questions.prompt: A common-envelope episode in an interacting binary can…
choices: remove a shared envelope and substantially shrink the orbit
guarantee the binary becomes unbound
occur only between isolated single stars
questions.feedback: The companion and stellar core may spiral inward within an envelope; whether the system ejects the envelope or merges depends on the model and conditions.

questions.prompt: Why might simulated systems have different statistical weights?
choices: Some simulated systems may represent different fractions of the underlying population
Physical masses must always equal weights
Weights guarantee every binary has the same formation history
questions.feedback: Weights can account for the simulated sampling procedure or the fraction of the model population represented by different systems.

questions.prompt: In an isolated Newtonian two-body system, negative total orbital energy (relative to zero at infinite separation) indicates…
choices: a bound orbit
a necessarily circular orbit
an unbound hyperbolic orbit
questions.feedback: Negative orbital energy implies a bound Keplerian orbit in this ideal model, but the eccentricity need not be zero.

questions.prompt: Binary mass transfer can occur when…
choices: one star's material flows toward its companion, for example through Roche-lobe overflow
the stars exchange only photons and no matter
the orbital separation is always infinite
questions.feedback: Matter can move from donor to accretor during binary interactions, with stability and outcomes depending on system properties.

questions.prompt: A reproducible scientific research question should ideally…
choices: specify an issue that can be investigated with identifiable methods and evidence
be immune to any possible evidence
guarantee the investigator's preferred answer
questions.feedback: Useful research questions identify a tractable uncertainty and a route to evaluate competing explanations or results.
